findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how blast-radius GLOBS are made current at currency-evaluation time so a NEWLY-created file under a glob invalidates: either record the glob PATTERNS in the signed manifest and re-enumerate matches at currency time (an ls, not a diff walker), or hash a directory-listing digest per glob, since the per-recorded-path re-hash cannot detect a file that did not exist at signing.
evidence: dependency_hashes returns `{p: _hash_file(p, base=base) for p in sorted(paths)}` — a concrete path set, no glob storage
compute_validity: `deps = manifest_deps(auth_manifest)` then re-hashes `for p, digest in sorted(deps.items())` — only recorded paths are checked

_hash_file docstring: 'A missing/unreadable path hashes to _ABSENT_HASH so a later create/delete is itself a detectable change' — create-detection works ONLY for paths already recorded as absent, which a glob does not enumerate
Plan lists directory globs (`criteria/**`, `reviewers/*.md`, `gates/*.yaml`) whose PURPOSE is to catch additions to those directories, but the named check cannot see additions
findings.finding: The blast-radius entries are GLOBS, but the reused ADR-0002 currency check is per-recorded-path (dependency_hashes stores concrete {path:sha256}; compute_validity re-hashes only those exact paths, with _hash_file mapping a missing path to _ABSENT_HASH). A glob expands to the files that exist at SIGNING time; a file newly CREATED under a blast-radius glob after review is never enumerated, gets no dep line, and its appearance is invisible to the per-path re-hash — so the design under-guards exactly the new-file churn the globs are meant to catch.
findings.location: Plan §Plan (b) ('evaluated by the SAME per-path content-hash currency check ADR 0002 already ships'; 'no new diff walker'); mechanism at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:324-352 (dependency_hashes) and 437, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:568-584 (compute_validity), _hash_file at manifest.py:175-185
scenarios: A no-file-impact review signs; later a new criterion file src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria/new_rule.md is added (no existing recorded path changes) — the attestation stays 'current' though a watched blast-radius directory grew.
A new reviewer prompt src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_NEW.md is added post-review — invisible to the per-path re-hash.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the blast-radius glob PATTERNS (not just their signing-time expansions) in the signed manifest, and at currency time re-enumerate each glob against the current gate ref and hash the sorted (path, sha256) listing — so an added/removed file under the glob changes the listing digest and invalidates. Keep the file_impact/cited/read-set members on the existing per-path check unchanged.

findings.finding: The read-set is recorded in the unsigned sidecar payload, but the currency/drift evaluation modified by component (b) (compute_validity) sources its drift basis exclusively from the authenticated signed manifest; the plan does not name where currency reads the read-set, nor reconcile the signed-vs-unsigned channel.

The 'small fixed blast-radius list (criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config)' is named only conceptually; the plan does not resolve these to concrete repo paths, so the blast-radius targets cannot be existence-checked or reproduced by an implementer.

Component (b) gates the authenticated `stale-head` invalidation trigger on a read-set persisted in the UNSIGNED sidecar payload (a), so an empty/tampered read-set yields an empty intersection and keeps the attestation current across arbitrary code drift — a fail-OPEN outcome WEAKER than the status quo, contradicting the plan's own promise that 'the fail-safe is never weaker than the status quo'. The plan does not name where currency evaluation reads the read-set nor bind that basis to the signed/authenticated channel.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the read-set into the SIGNED plan-review manifest (as the dep map already is), or treat any read-set sourced from the unsigned sidecar as 'basis unknown' -> fail-safe invalidate; only an authenticated, present read-set may narrow the trigger.

findings.finding: The plan proposes a novel invalidation-trigger scoping mechanism that overlaps two shipped systems it never cites — ADR-0002's content-addressed file_impact∪cited-paths dependency scoping and the bug-5e40 DRIFT floor's citation-intersected `git diff --name-only base..head` — and specifically modifies the whole-HEAD invalidation TRIGGER that ADR-0052 records was 'rejected as a security regression'; prior art is neither considered nor distinguished.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan (approved components a + b)', item (b) 'Diff-intersect on drift'; Context paragraph

findings.finding: The fixed blast-radius list is named by category ('criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config') rather than by concrete file paths or globs, leaving the executor to decide which files constitute each category — a data-design ambiguity in the load-bearing set that determines invalidation.
findings.location: Plan component (b): 'a small fixed blast-radius list: criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the category names with the concrete repo paths/globs that back each (state them in the plan and assert them in the AC2/AC3 tests).

findings.finding: The codebase already contains a Pass-3 DRIFT floor (bug 5e40, drift_floor.py) that solves the same unscoped-plan / code-drifted regime by intersecting novel-finding citations with `git diff --name-only signed_sha..HEAD` at the re-review OUTCOME layer, explicitly leaving the whole-HEAD invalidation TRIGGER untouched for security. The plan proposes the intersection at the TRIGGER layer (compute_validity) without acknowledging or relating to this existing mechanism — a structurally different, higher-blast-radius seam that overlaps it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the derivation protocol that reduces distinct_fetches to the signed read-set: which tools contribute paths (e.g. read_file only), how search_files query/pattern targets and list_directory directory targets are excluded or mapped, and that only existing repo-relative file paths enter the ADR-0002 per-path hash set.
evidence: Plan (a): 'The agentic passes already observe which repository files they open (distinct_fetches in telemetry). Persist that read-set (repo-relative paths only)'

ADR-0002 (docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md:27) consumes a per-path {path: content-hash} map of whole-file hashes, requiring repo-relative FILE paths
findings.finding: The read-set schema is fed into the ADR-0002 per-path content-hash check as 'repo-relative paths only', but the plan never specifies the protocol that derives those paths from the agentic passes' observation telemetry (distinct_fetches), which mixes path targets with non-path targets.
findings.location: Plan component (a) 'Record the review's read-set INSIDE the signed material' and (b) 'Feed the read-set into the ADR-0002 dependency set'
scenarios: A pass calls search_files (target='def foo') and list_directory (target='src/rebar/llm/'); the executor must decide whether these enter the dependency set and, if so, how a query or directory maps to a whole-file content hash
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to component (a) pinning the rule, e.g.: 'The read-set is the set of distinct_fetches entries whose tool is read_file (path-bearing); search_files query targets and list_directory directory targets are excluded — only repo-relative file paths that resolve to a hashable file enter the ADR-0002 dependency set.'
